descriptors.concept_name: Objective of Non-Current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations
descriptors.definition: The standard specifies the accounting, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements for non-current assets held for sale and discontinued operations. This segregation helps users evaluate an entity's future cash flows, earnings capacity, and financial position by separating them from continuing operations.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between ongoing operational activities and assets whose value is recovered principally through a sale transaction.

descriptors.concept_name: Scope of Non-Current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations
descriptors.definition: The classification and presentation rules apply to all recognized non-current assets and disposal groups, while measurement rules apply generally with specific exclusions. Assets scoped out from measurement under this standard include deferred tax assets, employee benefit assets, financial assets, biological assets, and insurance contracts.
terminology: Fair value less costs to sell
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general non-current assets subject to full standard rules and specific asset categories governed by separate financial standards.

descriptors.definition: Key terms include cash-generating units, components of an entity, costs to distribute, costs to sell, and disposal groups utilized throughout the standard. These definitions establish boundaries for identifying separable operations, associated disposal costs, and asset groupings transferred in a single transaction.
exclusion: General operational definitions outside the scope of non-current asset disposal
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes individual operational assets from multi-asset disposal groups and cash-generating units.

descriptors.concept_name: Classification of Non-Current Assets as Held for Sale
descriptors.definition: An entity must classify a non-current asset or disposal group as held for sale if its carrying amount will be recovered principally through a sale transaction rather than continuing use. The asset must be available for immediate sale in its present condition, and the sale must be highly probable.
inclusion: Non-current assets available for immediate sale
Disposal groups meeting high probability criteria
exclusion: Current assets sold individually outside a disposal group
Assets held for distant future sale
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes assets utilized continuously in operations from assets held exclusively for immediate recovery through sale.

descriptors.definition: An asset or disposal group must be ready for sale in its current condition with only normal and customary terms for such sales. Assets are not available for immediate sale if they remain vital to ongoing operations or require substantial value-enhancing refurbishments prior to disposal.
inclusion: Assets transferable under standard customary sales terms
exclusion: Assets delayed by operational dependencies or enhancement renovations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes customary transitional delays from intentional operational retention or pre-sale value enhancement.

descriptors.definition: A highly probable sale requires management commitment, active marketing at reasonable prices, an active buyer search, and an expected completion within one year without significant plan withdrawal likelihood. Shareholder approval requirements must also be evaluated for feasibility within this assessment.
exclusion: Tentative plans without active marketing or management commitment
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes general management intentions to sell from concrete, highly probable execution plans meeting rigorous procedural criteria.

descriptors.concept_name: Other Key Points and Exceptions to One-Year Period
descriptors.definition: Loss of control in a subsidiary requires classifying all its assets and liabilities as held for sale in consolidated statements regardless of retained non-controlling interests. The one-year completion period can be exceeded if delays stem from events beyond the entity's control and there is sufficient evidence of continued sales commitment.
inclusion: Beyond-control delay circumstances satisfying the one-year exception
exclusion: Delays caused by internal management indecision or controllable factors
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes entity-controlled delays from external, unforeseeable impediments permitting timeframe extensions.

descriptors.concept_name: Measurement of Non-Current Assets Classified as Held for Sale
descriptors.definition: Non-current assets or disposal groups classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of their carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. Costs to sell expected beyond one year are discounted to present value, with time-value increases recognized as financing costs in profit or loss.
terminology: Fair value less costs to sell
inclusion: Measurement at lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell
Present value adjustments for extended disposal periods
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard operational asset valuation models from the lower-of-carrying-amount and fair-value-less-costs-to-sell rule.

descriptors.concept_name: Measurement at Lower of Carrying Amount and Fair Value Less Costs to Sell
descriptors.definition: Assets held for sale are remeasured prior to classification and subsequently evaluated at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. Newly acquired assets meeting the criteria are initially measured at what their carrying amount would have been or fair value less costs to sell if acquired in a business combination.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard asset acquisition measurement from initial held-for-sale criteria application.

descriptors.concept_name: Recognition of Impairment Losses and Reversals
descriptors.definition: Impairment losses are recognized for initial or subsequent write-downs to fair value less costs to sell, while subsequent gains are recognized up to the cumulative impairment previously recorded. Depreciation and amortization of the asset cease immediately upon classification as held for sale.
inclusion: Impairment loss allocation starting with goodwill
exclusion: Interest and liability-associated expenses which continue to be recognized
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes the suspension of depreciation for held-for-sale assets from active operational asset depreciation models.

descriptors.concept_name: Changes to a Plan of Sale
descriptors.definition: When an asset or disposal group no longer meets held-for-sale criteria, it ceases to be classified as such and is measured at the lower of its pre-classification carrying amount adjusted for intervening depreciation and its recoverable amount. Adjustments are included in continuing operations profit or loss.
inclusion: Reclassification out of held for sale status
Carrying amount adjustments for missed depreciation
exclusion: Retroactive adjustments violating standard transition rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes active held-for-sale assets from assets reverting to operational use due to cancelled sale plans.

descriptors.concept_name: Presentation and Disclosures of Non-Current Assets Held for Sale
descriptors.definition: Non-current assets and disposal group assets and liabilities held for sale must be presented separately on the balance sheet without offsetting them against each other. Major classes of these assets and liabilities must be disclosed, and comparative balance sheet amounts for prior periods are not re-presented.
inclusion: Separate balance sheet presentation of assets and liabilities
Disclosure of major asset and liability classes
exclusion: Offsetting assets against liabilities as a single net amount
Re-presentation of prior period comparative balance sheets
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes current presentation requirements from prior period balance sheet comparative restatement rules.
